[h2]Verdict[/h2]
✅ Recommended

One of the best co-op games on the market, and a great choice even for people who do not usually play games.

[h2]My history with the game[/h2]
I currently have 17.6 hours in It Takes Two on Steam.

I started playing it for the second time back in January, but I have not continued for a while because it is not always easy to find time with another player and finish a co-op game together.

Maybe I will finish this second playthrough one day, but even now I can say that this is a very good game.

[h2]Quick signals[/h2]
💸 Value: ✅ Worth it
🖥️ Requirements: ✅ Reasonable
🎨 Graphics: ✅ Beautiful and colorful
⏱️ Length: ✅ Good co-op campaign length
📖 Story: ✅ Simple, emotional, and fun
🎮 Gameplay: ✅ Excellent co-op variety
🐛 Bugs: ✅ No major issues for me

[h2]What I liked[/h2]

* It is one of the best games for two players.
* The co-op design is the main strength of the whole experience.
* Every section brings something new, so the gameplay does not feel repetitive.
* It is fun, creative, colorful, and very easy to enjoy with another person.
* The game works well for both gamers and non-gamers.
* It is a great choice if you want to play something together instead of just watching someone else play.
* The variety of mechanics makes the whole journey feel fresh.

[h2]What didn’t work for me[/h2]

* You really need another person to properly play it.
* Because of that, it can be harder to finish if both players do not have time.
* This is not the kind of game you can easily continue whenever you want alone.
* My second playthrough has been paused for a long time because of scheduling.

[h2]Is it an endless game? How long to beat?[/h2]
No, this is not an endless game.

It is a full co-op story campaign. I currently have 17.6 hours played, and depending on your pace, experience, and how much you explore or repeat sections, your playtime can vary.

[h2]Who will love it[/h2]
You will probably enjoy It Takes Two if you want a great co-op game, especially with a partner, friend, sibling, or someone who does not usually play many games.

It is one of those rare games that can be recommended to both regular players and casual/non-gamers.

[h2]Replay value[/h2]
Replay value is decent, especially if you want to experience it again with a different person.

For me, I already started a second playthrough, but I have not finished it yet because finding time with another player is the real challenge.

[h2]Final note[/h2]
It Takes Two is a very good co-op game and easily one of the best choices for two players.

I have not finished my second playthrough yet, but the game is creative, fun, polished, and enjoyable even for people who are not hardcore gamers.

Recommended to gamers and non-gamers alike.

⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ WHAT A GAME!

I played It Takes Two with a friend, and honestly… I didn't expect to love it this much.

We're used to jumping into FPS games and shooting swarms of enemies, so playing a co-op game that's basically the complete opposite was such a refreshing change. And somehow, it was just as much fun — if not more.

The gameplay is smooth, creative, and ridiculously fun. The puzzles were clever and interesting without feeling like a chore, and every chapter brought something new. Each level felt fresh, exciting, and different enough that I was constantly wondering, "Alright… what are they gonna make us do next?"

And the story? Beautiful. Sweet. Funny. And surprisingly emotional. ❤️

The ending was so perfect that my buddy and I might've even shed a man tear. 😂

🌿 Favorite level: The Garden.
Absolutely loved that section.

One thing worth mentioning: I'm color blind, and this game is definitely NOT color-blind friendly. 😂 There were definitely moments where I was sitting there thinking, "Okay… which color am I supposed to be looking at?!" But I still made it through the entire game, so don't let that stop you.

I've got 17 hours played, and I can honestly say I highly recommend this game to anyone who's a decent gamer and just wants to have a TON of fun with a friend.

10/10 — seriously, play this game.

And remember… It Takes Two.

Apparently it also takes two grown men, 17 hours, and an emotional ending to discover we actually have feelings. 😂

Worth all the praise. One thing I'll say, though, is that it's not quite as beginner-friendly as people make it out to be.

If you're in a relationship with a non-gamer and you're thinking this might be the game that finally lures them in, I'm not going to say don't do it, but maybe keep your expectations in check and be mindful that it may not work.

It's not particularly difficult, but the game does assume both players have at least a fair understanding of how to use a controller: handling movement and camera simultaneously, working buttons and triggers together, etc.
It's not really a game where one player can carry the other. Progress requires both players to know what they're doing, especially during boss fights. If one person is mostly lost, you're going to get stuck.

That said, that's also what makes the game so much fun. The fact that you both have to work together to progress means neither player can just sit back and let the other do everything. You have to pull your own weight.

So if one of you has literally never held a game controller before, It Takes Two might not be the magical portal into gaming together you've been hoping for. Worth a shot, but be aware that you could easily end up giving up after an hour.

So I ended up playing it with a mate and had a fantastic time. It was admittedly pretty funny having two dudes work through a married couple's divorce/reconciliation process together, but hey, who said men can't share their feelings.

And let's face it, this isn't really a game you're playing for the story anyway. The whole divorce/reconciliation thing is a cute gimmick, but it's the gameplay that makes It Takes Two amazing. There's a ton of variety, and the constant need to cooperate in different ways just keeps things endlessly fun.
